summary: This article explains how traditional silver jewelry is crafted and worn in Saudi Arabia, the skill of silversmiths, and how designs carry regional identity.
introduce: Show the title “Traditional Saudi Jewelry” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a craftsman who makes things out of silver
a delicate pattern made from thin, twisted wire
a custom passed down through many years

challengeTerms.def: traditions, objects, or culture passed down from earlier generations
a person learning a skilled trade from an experienced worker

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a handmade piece of traditional jewelry is more special than a similar piece bought brand new today? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why silver jewelry patterns differ from region to region in Saudi Arabia.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review silversmith, filigree, and tradition, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses heritage, intricate, and apprentice to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
